name: Rome
tagline: Four ways to eat the perfect carbonara, from a tiny Trastevere trattoria to a rooftop with three Michelin stars.

La Pergola.description: Heinz Beck's cuisine on the rooftop of the Waldorf Astoria Cavalieri, overlooking all of Rome. Three Michelin stars for two decades now.

Armando al Pantheon.description: A historic reference for Roman cuisine next to the Pantheon, with one of the city's best carbonaras.

Trattoria Pennestri.description: A neighborhood trattoria in Ostiense with carbonara, cacio e pepe, amatriciana, and gricia. Bib Gourmand.

Da Enzo al 29.description: A tiny Trastevere trattoria, always with a line, famous for its perfectly balanced carbonara.

Salumeria Roscioli.description: A delicatessen and wine cellar with more than 2,800 wines, next to Campo de' Fiori. Anthony Bourdain ate here in the Rome special of "Parts Unknown"; its carbonara is recognized by 50 Top Italy.

Il Pagliaccio.description: Chef Anthony Genovese's creative kitchen on Via dei Banchi Vecchi, holding two Michelin stars in the 2026 guide.

Enoteca La Torre.description: Domenico Stile's restaurant inside Villa Laetitia on the Tiber, promoted to two Michelin stars in the 2026 guide.

Acquolina.description: Chef Daniele Lippi's seafood-focused fine dining at The First Roma Arte hotel, near Piazza del Popolo. Two Michelin stars.

Pulejo.description: Intimate fine dining in Prati from chef Davide Pulejo, who trained at Il Convivio Troiani and Noma; one Michelin star.

Orma Roma.description: Colombian-Italian chef Roy Caceres blends Latin American, Asian and Mediterranean ingredients near Via Veneto. One Michelin star.

INEO.description: Modern Roman cuisine from chef Heros De Agostinis at the Anantara Palazzo Naiadi hotel, on Piazza della Repubblica. One Michelin star.

Pipero Roma.description: Chef Alessandro Pipero brings his refined Roman cuisine to Corso Vittorio Emanuele II; one Michelin star since 2012.

Il Convivio Troiani.description: The Troiani brothers have served refined Italian cuisine on a quiet street near Piazza Navona since 1990. One Michelin star.

Per Me by Giulio Terrinoni.description: Chef Giulio Terrinoni signs a creative seafood-driven menu near Campo de' Fiori. One Michelin star.

Achilli al Parlamento.description: A long-running institution near the Italian Parliament that earned its first Michelin star in 2025 under chef Pierluigi Gallo.

Imàgo.description: Set atop the Hotel Hassler with views over the Spanish Steps; one Michelin star.

Moma Restaurant.description: Modern restaurant near Piazza Barberini born from a project by young Italian chefs; one Michelin star.

La Terrazza.description: The Hotel Eden's rooftop dining room overlooks Rome from Via Ludovisi; it earned its Michelin star in the 2026 guide.

Marco Martini Restaurant.description: Chef Marco Martini reinterprets Roman cuisine through a contemporary lens on Viale Aventino; one Michelin star.

Aroma.description: On the rooftop of Palazzo Manfredi, with the Colosseum almost within reach; one Michelin star under chef Giuseppe Di Iorio.

All'Oro.description: Chef Riccardo Di Giacinto reinvents Roman classics like carbonara at The H'All Tailor Suite hotel near Piazza del Popolo. One Michelin star.

Glass Hostaria.description: Chef Cristina Bowerman offers creative Italian cuisine in a design-forward space in the heart of Trastevere; one Michelin star.

Zia.description: A small Trastevere restaurant where chef Antonio Ziantoni signs a personal take on Italian cuisine; one Michelin star.

Idylio by Apreda.description: Chef Francesco Apreda, trained across Asia, leads the kitchen at the Ambasciatori Palace hotel on Via Veneto; one Michelin star.

Checchino dal 1887.description: Open beside Testaccio's old slaughterhouse since 1887, specializing in Roman offal cuisine: oxtail stew, tripe, and rigatoni alla pajata.

Flavio al Velavevodetto.description: A Testaccio trattoria built into the ancient Monte dei Cocci pottery mound, serving textbook cacio e pepe, amatriciana and carbonara.

Perilli.description: A family-run Testaccio trattoria open since 1911, with checkered tablecloths and one of Rome's most traditional carbonaras.

Felice a Testaccio.description: A long-running Testaccio family trattoria famous for tossing cacio e pepe tableside inside a wheel of pecorino cheese.

Da Oio a Casa Mia.description: A no-frills Testaccio trattoria loyal to old-school Roman cooking: amatriciana, tripe, and roast lamb.

Cesare al Casaletto.description: A neighborhood trattoria in Monteverde, off the tourist trail, praised by food critics for its carbonara and fried starters.

Trattoria Der Pallaro.description: Near Campo de' Fiori, offering a fixed no-menu meal for decades that walks diners through classic Roman dishes.

Hostaria Antica Roma.description: On the Via Appia Antica among Roman catacombs, serving a menu inspired by recipes from classical antiquity.

Trattoria Monti.description: A family-run trattoria in the Monti district bringing cuisine from the Marche region to Rome, with vincisgrassi lasagna as its signature dish.

Dar Poeta.description: A benchmark Trastevere pizzeria known for its long-fermented dough and near-permanent line out front.

Ai Marmi.description: A classic Roman pizzeria on Viale di Trastevere nicknamed 'the morgue' for its marble-slab tables; thin, crackly-crust pizza.

Ivo a Trastevere.description: One of Trastevere's historic pizzerias, open since the 1960s, with a wood-fired oven and tables that stay full.

Pizzeria Da Remo.description: A Testaccio icon for paper-thin Roman-style pizza; loud, communal tables and lines that spill onto the street.

Antico Forno Roscioli.description: The Roscioli family's bakery and pizza-by-the-slice counter on Via dei Chiavari, with critically acclaimed sourdough bread and pizza bianca.

Forno Campo de' Fiori.description: A historic bakery right on Campo de' Fiori, famous for its freshly baked pizza bianca.

Trapizzino.description: Chef Stefano Callegari invented the trapizzino here in 2008: a triangle of pizza bianca stuffed with Roman braises like oxtail stew or hunter's chicken.

Supplizio.description: A tiny shop near Campo de' Fiori devoted entirely to supplì, Rome's deep-fried rice croquette stuffed with mozzarella.

Pizzarium Bonci.description: Baker Gabriele Bonci sells airy, seasonally topped pizza by the slice in Prati. Anthony Bourdain sampled it, including his Hawaiian-style pie, in the Rome episode of 'Parts Unknown'.

Domenico dal 1968.description: A family-run Testaccio trattoria open since 1968, awarded the Michelin Bib Gourmand for its no-frills, product-driven Roman cooking.

Hosteria Grappolo d'Oro.description: A hostaria near Campo de' Fiori holding the Michelin Bib Gourmand for seasonal Roman cooking at fair prices.

Piperno.description: A historic restaurant in the Jewish Ghetto, open since the 19th century, famous for its crisp carciofi alla giudia (fried artichokes).

Nonna Betta.description: A Ghetto trattoria specializing in Roman-Jewish cuisine, with fried artichokes and battered salt-cod fillets among its staples.

Ba'Ghetto.description: A kosher restaurant on Via del Portico d'Ottavia blending Roman-Jewish and North African cooking.

Sora Margherita.description: A tiny, informal Ghetto trattoria that for years had no visible sign, a reference point for home-style Roman-Jewish cooking.

Da Giggetto al Portico d'Ottavia.description: Set beside the ruins of the Portico d'Ottavia, a Ghetto institution since 1923 for Jewish-style artichokes and Roman cooking.

Pasticceria Boccione.description: An old, barely-marked Ghetto bakery famous for its torta di ricotta e visciole, a ricotta and sour-cherry tart.

Trattoria Sora Lella.description: On Tiber Island, founded by actress Elena Fabrizi ('Sora Lella'); Anthony Bourdain ate suppli, meatballs and offal here in the Rome episode of 'Parts Unknown'.

Il Goccetto.description: A historic wine bar on Via dei Banchi Vecchi, with hundreds of labels and cheese-and-charcuterie boards to match.

Cul de Sac.description: One of Rome's earliest modern wine bars, just off Piazza Navona, with a wine list that has run for pages since the 1970s.

Litro.description: A natural-wine bar in Monteverde with market-driven small plates and one of Rome's most carefully curated natural wine lists.

Antica Pesa.description: A historic Trastevere restaurant, open since 1922 in a former public weighing station, serving classic Roman food with a notable wine cellar.

La Rosetta.description: A long-standing reference for seafood cooking in Rome, near the Pantheon, running since the 1960s.

Pierluigi.description: A seafood restaurant with a terrace on a hidden square between the Ghetto and Campo de' Fiori, open since 1938.

Il Sanlorenzo.description: Elegant seafood cooking inside a 15th-century palazzo near Campo de' Fiori, with raw fish preparations as a specialty.

Antico Arco.description: Perched atop the Gianicolo hill, a pioneer of contemporary Italian cooking in Rome since the late 1990s.

Roma Sparita.description: A Trastevere trattoria famous for serving cacio e pepe inside an edible basket of baked parmesan, an image widely shared on social media.

Spirito DiVino.description: Housed in a former Trastevere synagogue, serving dishes inspired by recipes from Imperial and Republican Rome.

Colline Emiliane.description: A family-run restaurant near Piazza Barberini specializing in fresh pasta and Emilia-Romagna cooking since 1931.

Al Moro.description: An old-guard trattoria near the Trevi Fountain, open since 1929, a favorite of classic Roman society.

Osteria Fernanda.description: A contemporary Italian osteria in the less touristy end of Trastevere, well regarded by Roman food critics.

Casa Coppelle.description: A romantic-feeling restaurant on Piazza delle Coppelle blending Italian and French cooking.

Ditirambo.description: Near Campo de' Fiori, Roman and Italian cooking built on organic, market-driven ingredients since 1996.

Necci dal 1924.description: A Pigneto bar-trattoria opened in 1924, once frequented by Pier Paolo Pasolini and today a neighborhood gathering spot.

Seu Pizza Illuminati.description: A designer pizzeria near Trastevere using specialty flours and seasonal toppings, a benchmark of Rome's new-wave pizza scene.

La Gatta Mangiona.description: A Monteverde pizzeria highly rated for its light doughs and creative topping combinations.

Sforno.description: A pizzeria in the San Giovanni district that pioneered long-fermentation dough in Rome.

180g Pizzeria Romana.description: A Prati pizzeria focused on thin, crisp Roman-style round pizza made with locally sourced ingredients.

Pinsere.description: A small shop near Termini station specializing in Roman pinsa, the oval, airy cousin of pizza.

Gelateria Giolitti.description: A historic gelateria near the Pantheon, open since 1900 and one of Rome's oldest and most visited.

Fatamorgana.description: An artisanal gelato chain with several Rome locations (this one in Monti), known for inventive dairy-free and gluten-free flavors.

Gelateria dei Gracchi.description: A Prati gelateria using quality ingredients and intensely fruity flavors, a modern classic of the city.

Otaleg.description: A Trastevere gelateria from gelato master Marco Radicioni; its name is 'gelato' spelled backwards.

San Crispino.description: A historic gelateria near the Trevi Fountain, a pioneer of preservative-free artisanal gelato in Rome.

Fassi - Palazzo del Freddo.description: Rome's oldest gelateria, founded in 1880 in the Esquilino district, set in a vintage-style hall.

Frigidarium.description: A popular gelateria near Piazza Navona, known for gelato coated in tempered chocolate right at the counter.

Sant'Eustachio Il Caffè.description: A historic coffee bar near the Pantheon, open since 1938, famous for its foamy espresso made with a secret recipe.

Tazza d'Oro.description: A coffee roastery and bar next to the Pantheon since 1946, famous for its coffee granita topped with cream.

Antico Caffè Greco.description: Rome's oldest café, opened in 1760 on Via Condotti, historically frequented by Goethe, Byron and Casanova.

Barnum Cafe.description: A vintage-styled café near Campo de' Fiori, popular for breakfast, brunch, and laptop work.

Mercato di Testaccio.description: Testaccio's covered market hall, with fresh-produce stalls and some of Rome's best street-food bites.

Mercato Trionfale.description: Rome's largest food market, in Prati, with hundreds of stalls selling produce, fish and cheese.

Mordi e Vai.description: A stall inside the Mercato di Testaccio famous for sandwiches built on Roman offal, like tongue or garofolato beef stew.

Er Buchetto.description: A tiny shop near Termini station specializing in porchetta sandwiches, eaten standing up, no frills.

Pastificio Guerra.description: A former pasta shop near the Spanish Steps, now famous for serving a bargain-priced daily pasta dish that has gone viral on social media.

Regoli.description: A historic Esquilino pastry shop since 1916, famous for its cream-filled maritozzo bun.

Mercato Centrale Roma.description: A food hall inside Termini train station, with stalls run by respected Roman artisans and chefs.

Eataly Roma Ostiense.description: A large Eataly outpost in Ostiense's former train station, with shops, restaurants and regional Italian products.

Hostaria Da Cesare.description: A classic Prati trattoria serving traditional Roman cooking alongside seafood dishes, running for decades.

Tonnarello.description: A very popular Trastevere trattoria with tables spilling onto the street and generous portions of Roman pasta.

Le Mani in Pasta.description: A Trastevere trattoria appreciated for its handmade fresh pasta and daily fish specials.

Da Teo.description: A Trastevere trattoria on Piazza dei Ponziani, with outdoor seating and straightforward Roman cooking.

Osteria dell'Ingegno.description: A casual osteria near the Pantheon with market-driven Italian food and a solid by-the-glass wine list.

Enoteca Ferrara.description: A Trastevere wine bar and restaurant with more than thirty years of history and an extensive Italian wine list.

Bir & Fud.description: A Trastevere gastropub that pioneered Italian craft beer in Rome, pairing it with Neapolitan-style pizza and fried starters.

L'Arcangelo.description: A Prati restaurant from chef Arcangelo Dandini, reinterpreting classic Roman offal cooking with modern touches.

Volpetti.description: A benchmark delicatessen and cheese shop in Testaccio since 1973, with a carefully curated selection of Italian cured meats and cheeses.
